text:
hannah: heads up — trying to run acceptance tests that call local redwoodctl inside a Docker container and ran into config/token confusion. container runs `redwoodctl local serve` but it keeps using an old token baked into the image. any tips for a clean dev flow?

mark: you should avoid baking ~/.redwood into the image. mount a config volume at /root/.redwood or pass REDWOOD_TOKEN at runtime.

hannah: tried mounting but docker-compose.yml had a named volume that pointed to a host directory with stale config. compose file snippet: `volumes: - redwood-config:/root/.redwood` and `volumes: { redwood-config: ./ci/redwood }` so it copied the old config during build.

rui: two lessons: 1) use an entrypoint that validates token freshness and exits non-zero with a helpful message if token invalid 2) support `redwoodctl profiles import --from-stdin` so CI can pipe secrets without writeable volumes. filed DX-630.

hannah: for now I solved by adding `entrypoint: ["/bin/sh","-c","if [ -n \"$REDWOOD_TOKEN\" ]; then mkdir -p /root/.redwood && cat > /root/.redwood/config.yaml <<YAML
profiles:
  ci:
    token: \"$REDWOOD_TOKEN\"
current_profile: ci
YAML
fi; exec redwoodctl local serve --host 127.0.0.1"]` which is inelegant but works.

mark: also watch for file permission mismatch when mounting from mac host into Linux container (uid/gid). redwoodctl will fail to write the KV cache. workaround: `chown` the host dir to the container UID as part of entrypoint.

docs-bot: added CI patterns to devex/cli/ci.md: avoid baking config in images, prefer env token or `profiles import` from a secret store, chown mounted dir, and use `--host 127.0.0.1` for containerized local serve.

ci-bot: created issue DX-630: profiles-import-stdin and DX-631: entrypoint-token-check.

hannah: thanks — once I switched to REDWOOD_TOKEN from secret manager the tests run cleanly and we can build immutable images without leaking tokens. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
